caller_census.method: byte-level .text scan for e8/e9 rel32 targeting 0x514bf60, cross-checked against a linear objdump -d sweep of the whole binary; both methods agree on exactly these 11 call sites and no tail jumps
caller_census.other_sites_note: the ten non-self sites' enclosing functions are census only and are not modelled here; the self site 0x514bf77 is the child recursion inside the function itself

notes: Instruction-level detail lives only in the raw objdump excerpts; this JSON holds semantic records only.

This function has no endbr64: its first instruction is the null test at 0x514bf60. The nopl at 0x514bfcd is genuine alignment padding before the null-path ret at 0x514bfd0, which is inside the FDE range; the 15 int3 bytes from 0x514bfd1 to the next FDE at 0x514bfe0 are padding, verified byte-for-byte.
objdump's nearest-symbol annotation for this address range is explicitly not claimed as a symbol name; the function is identified by its FDE range and bytes only.
The +0x00 and +0x08 qwords of the node are never read by this function and are not claimed.

The string layout is read as the libstdc++ SSO shape (pointer, length unread, capacity-or-inline-buffer) because the disposal test compares the pointer against the inline-buffer address and the delete size is the buffer field + 1; the source-level type name is not claimed.

The loop-back branch at 0x514bfc4 targets 0x514bf70, which precedes the mov %rbp,%rbx at 0x514bf70, so the next-sibling pointer IS reloaded into rbx on every iteration; the first entry bypasses that mov via the jmp at 0x514bf6e because rbx already holds the input object.

The next-sibling pointer is saved into rbp at 0x514bf84 before any disposal, so disposing a node cannot break the walk; the child pointer is read fresh from [rbx+0x18] on each iteration after the sibling reload.
The ten external call sites are recorded as a census only; their enclosing functions (in the 0x5153xxx-0x5157xxx region) are not modelled, and no reachability beyond direct calls is claimed for them.

The following FDE at 0x514bfe0 is a different function and is not claimed here; the preceding FDE at 0x514bdf0 is the string build-and-move function bound by open PR #1358, and this item does not re-claim it.

plt_delete.stub_note: the GOT slot's file bytes are the stub's own lazy-binding resolver entry (0x5660446), not a resolved symbol address, exactly as in the list-teardown packet

rule.arguments: rdi = node pointer or null; void return
rule.child: for each node, before its own disposal, recurse on [node+0x18]; a null child returns immediately via the je at 0x514bf63 to the ret at 0x514bfd0
rule.disposal_order_per_node: child recursion, then the +0x40 string, then the +0x20 string, then the node itself
rule.next: after a node's disposal, advance to the sibling saved from [node+0x10] before disposal; a null saved sibling ends the walk
rule.null_input: a null input returns immediately with no delete call
rule.self_delete: operator delete via PLT 0x5660440 with (node, 0x60) on every non-null node
rule.string_disposal: for each of the two strings: if [node+pointer_offset] == node+buffer_offset, the string is inline (SSO) and nothing is freed; otherwise operator delete via PLT 0x5660440 with (pointer, [node+buffer_offset]+1 mod 2^64)
